newsitem.title: FRANCE: NATO assembly picks U.S. Senator Roth as president.
newsitem.headline: NATO assembly picks U.S. Senator Roth as president.

text.p: The North Atlantic Assembly, a defence body grouping parliamentarians from 40 countries including NATO's 16 nations, elected U.S. Senator William Roth as its new president on Thursday.
The Assembly chose the Delaware Republican for a one-year term to succeed retiring German Social Democrat Karsten Voigt, who has headed NATO's parliamentary arm for two years.

Roth said his agenda would be to promote NATO's enlargement to admit the new democracies of Central Europe by 1999, assure those nations not among the first to join that enlargement would remain an open process, and establish a substantive Russia-NATO charter to develop cooperation with Moscow.
"This is a time for a NATO that reaches out and eventually includes all the democracies of Central and Eastern Europe," he said.

The Assembly also formally announced the departure of its Secretary-General Peter Corterier, who resigned after 10 years in office following criticism by U.S. Congressional auditors of the Brussels-based body's management.

Roth paid tribute to Corterier, a German Social Democrat who stood up against anti-nuclear pacifists in his own party, saying: "We should remember that at great risk to his own political career, Peter stood firm against those who sought to diminish or destroy the Alliance."
